title: Playing along online and slowing YouTube backing tracks
summary: No platform allows playing together without delay; students use Aebersold tracks on YouTube at slower speed. Both learn technology from students.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Are you — I don’t know what sort of platform you’re using but can you play with them at the same time?

I haven’t found a platform where you can do that. I do, but I know there’s always a delay. So I’m asking again, I’m asking the parents to try to have like a second device available so they can have something to play along with. In other words like I just discovered that on YouTube you can adjust the speed of the files.

Yeah, so they can go to a YouTube of a Jamey Aebersold, especially if it’s somebody playing along with it, then it doesn’t have to be me playing along, and they can slow that down if it’s too fast, and use it as a study tool. But if they use it on FaceTime on the same device then I can’t hear it.
I had to have a student hip me to that thing about YouTube.
Me too. A student just told me.
We learn a lot from our students these days.
